_theme_schema: A venue's `theme` block is everything about how that venue LOOKS. It is read
by VenueFloor.Theme (scenes/venue/floor/venue_floor.gd) and drawn through the
kind registry in scenes/venue/floor/exhibits.gd.
surround   name of a City style (scenes/venue/floor/city.gd): 'parkland' for
the natural-history hall, 'harbour' for the aquarium.
palette    key -> colour. Anything else in the theme can reference a key with
a token: '@trim', '@room.gallery|d10' (darkened 0.10),
'@floor|l14' (lightened 0.14). '@roomfloor.<room>' is the computed
floor colour of a room. Plain '#RRGGBB' is always allowed.
rooms      the floor plan. `rect` is [gx, gy, w, h] in TILES and is the only
thing that fixes where anything stands: every waypoint listed
inside a room def is RELATIVE to its rect origin, so moving a
rect moves the counters, the queue, the porters and the plaque
with it. `role` tells VenueFloor what fixtures the room needs:
queue | store | promo | exhibit | lobby | link.
walls      [{at, len, axis: x|y, col, h}] - back walls and low dividers.
shell      {inset, col} - the slab the whole building stands on.
exhibits   the things visitors come to look at. Each is a `kind` from the
registry plus its spec, an `anchor` (grid point it Y-sorts at),
and `views` - standing spots as OFFSETS from that anchor, which
is what stops browse spots drifting away from the exhibit they
belong to. `layer: wall` draws into the shared ground item.
props      furniture. Same shape, no views. `anchor` defaults to the centre
of the footprint; state it when a piece was tuned by eye.
dressing   floor / wall / ceiling decals, drawn into the ground canvas item
so a hundred of them cost a handful of draw calls.
extends    inherit another venue's theme and override whole top-level keys.
Venues 3-6 do this until their own themes are authored; venues 1
and 2 are authored in full and share nothing.

venues.name: Whispering Pines Hall
venues.desc: A dusty small-town exhibit hall. Every empire starts somewhere.

venues.name: Tidewater Aquarium
venues.desc: A working harbour aquarium: cold water, warm crowds, 750x the takings of the Pines.

venues.name: Grand River Athenaeum
venues.desc: A marble landmark drawing crowds from across the region.

venues.name: Sunspire Gallery
venues.desc: A desert icon of glass and gold, famous worldwide.

venues.name: Cloudrest Citadel
venues.desc: A mountain-top fortress of wonders above the clouds.

venues.name: Aurora World Museum
venues.desc: The definitive world-class institution. Legends queue here.

venues.name: Celestial Conservatory
venues.desc: A moonlit glasshouse whose orbital collection circles a living conservatory.

venues.name: Ironwood Citadel
venues.desc: A mountain fortress museum of armories, royal halls, and guarded treasure.

venues.name: Pelagic Crown
venues.desc: A vast ocean palace where abyssal wonders gather beneath a coral crown.

venues.name: Chronos Spire
venues.desc: A four-storey monument to time, machinery, and the civilizations between.

venues.name: Empyrean Palace
venues.desc: A monumental palace museum ascending through royal courts into the clouds.

venues.name: The Infinite Museum
venues.desc: The final world museum: every age, realm, and impossible collection in one.
